mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5% over the prior month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the previous 60-day period (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS trigger is active.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum measured by PAYEMS indicates labor market strength that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no correlation with PAYEMS changes (Pearson's rho < 0.2) or are worse than a flat labor market baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) suggests weakening aggregate demand, which lowers growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by 4% in the current quarter relative to the prior quarter
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from a period of stable industrial production (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence proxy (HOUST) signals tight supply conditions and risk aversion, interactionally depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Interaction term between INDPRO and HOUST is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) or 20-day forward returns are not lower than expected from each variable in isolation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds +2% in a month, it anticipates future inflation expectations that the Fed will treat with tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower when CPIAUCSL crosses +2% change threshold (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% suggests labor market tightening that supports equity risk pricing, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and remains below for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not higher than during the prior 60-day period of similar UNRATE levels (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (PAYEMS) above 130,000 suggest resilient consumer demand, which elevates growth expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during the prior 5-day window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) combined with a simultaneous rise in consumer spending (HOUST) creates conflicting signals that fail to resolve into a clear direction, leaving S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days unpredictable (no consistent sign).
failure_condition: Over the 20-day horizon, SPX forward returns show no statistically significant pattern relative to the prior 20-day window (p > 0.05 for both + and -).
